businessModel: GNOME Foundation donations and volunteer work
updateCadence: Follows GNOME releases every six months; WebKitGTK updated separately
summary: GNOME Web (Epiphany) is a clean GTK4/libadwaita browser on WebKitGTK. It has built-in ad blocking, web-app mode and Keyring integration, but minimal extensions, no working sync since GNOME 47, and Linux-only availability.
bestFor: Linux phones and small screens (adaptive UI)
People who want a simple, low-tracking browser

pros.title: GNOME-native
pros.detail: GTK4/libadwaita UI, GNOME Keyring and Wayland support.

pros.title: Web apps
pros.detail: Install any site as a standalone launcher.

pros.title: Built-in protection
pros.detail: WebKit content-blocker ad blocking, Intelligent Tracking Prevention and Safe Browsing.

pros.title: Sandboxed
pros.detail: Uses Bubblewrap sandboxing for tab processes.

pros.title: Zero telemetry
pros.detail: GNOME project with no accounts or tracking.

cons.title: Almost no extensions
cons.detail: Experimental WebExtensions in GNOME 43/44 only; the old extension package was removed.

cons.title: Sync disabled
cons.detail: Firefox Sync support was disabled in GNOME 47 after Mozilla’s changes.

cons.title: WebKitGTK compatibility
cons.detail: Some sites break compared with Blink; no mainstream DRM.

faq.q: Does GNOME Web sync with Firefox?
faq.a: No. Firefox Sync was supported from GNOME 3.26 to 47 but was disabled in GNOME 47.

faq.q: Can I use Chrome or Firefox extensions?
faq.a: No. Only an experimental subset of WebExtensions exists, and there is no add-on store.
I could not confirm; one GNOME 51 guide claims passkey support, but this is not corroborated.

timeline.event: Epiphany started as a lightweight GNOME browser
Experimental WebExtensions arrive in GNOME 43 (expanded in 44)

switching.note: Imports bookmarks, history and passwords from Chrome/Chromium and Firefox via the import dialog.

spec.drm: No mainstream DRM (Widevine unsupported in practice)

battery: Efficient but less tuned than Safari
extras: Web apps and Safe Browsing only

featureNotes.profiles: Web apps have own profiles; limited main profiles

unverified: Whether Firefox Sync was fully removed or only disabled
